question: A 70-year-old man comes to the physician because of right-sided back pain, red urine, and weight loss for the last 4 months. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 40 years. A CT scan of the abdomen shows a large right-sided renal mass. Biopsy of the mass shows polygonal clear cells filled with lipids. Which of the following features is necessary to determine the tumor grade in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Lipid-filled clear cells in renal mass -> Likely renal cell carcinoma -> Tumor grade determined by degree of mitotic activity -> 80%
CHAIN: Red urine and weight loss -> Suggestive of renal cell carcinoma -> Tumor grade determined by degree of mitotic activity -> 75%
CHAIN: Smoking history -> Increased risk for renal cell carcinoma -> Tumor grade determined by degree of mitotic activity -> 70%
analysis: In determining the tumor grade of the renal mass in this patient, the key feature necessary would be the degree of mitotic activity. Mitotic activity refers to the rate at which cells within the tumor are dividing and is a crucial factor in assessing the aggressiveness of the tumor.
